title: A Verifier Taxonomy and Open Benchmark for Detectability of LLM-Generated NetOps Failures — Preregistration
research_question: Can a machine-readable verifier taxonomy plus a public benchmark of LLM-generated network-change proposals reliably characterize which failure classes are detectably deterministic (syntax/policy/reachability/stateful) versus semantic (intent misalignment), and thereby guide deterministic verifier selection for NetOps workflows?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: A machine-readable verifier taxonomy (attributes: syntax, policy, reachability, stateful-emulation, intent-mapping) explains a nonzero fraction of variance in per-task deterministic-detectability (paired success-rate difference) across tasks (paired estimand described below).

H2: A stronger verifier class (syntax+policy+reachability/stateful) yields a higher detectability rate than a baseline lightweight syntax-only verifier by at least 0.15 (15 percentage points) on the preregistered confirmatory task set.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: Which specific injected or natural failure subclasses remain undetected by all deterministic verifier classes (taxonomy leaf-level analysis)?
EQ2: How sensitive are taxonomy-predicted detectability patterns to different hosted LLM generation prompts and seeds?
benchmark_scope: Publicly available, non-sensitive network configurations, change logs, and policy snippets (provably public GitHub repos, operator blog archives, RFC/standards examples).
Synthetic network-change tasks produced by hosted LLM API prompts (seeded) that inject controlled failure modes per injection protocol.
Taxonomy-labeled failure classes limited to: syntax, policy-violation, reachability-break, stateful-emulation-failure, ambiguous-intent / semantic-mismatch.
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the mean within-task difference in binary detection (1=detected by verifier-class, 0=not detected) where each task is evaluated under baseline verifier (syntax-only exemplar) and guarded verifier (syntax+policy+reachability/stateful exemplar).
secondary_estimands: per-verifier-class detection coverage (proportion detected) across confirmatory tasks (descriptive).
sensitivity analysis estimand: paired difference under failed_call_treatment=complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity.
sampling_plan: Paired within-task design, task_count = 100 confirmatory paired tasks. Each task = single network-change proposal (either natural from public corpus or LLM-generated proposal with injected failure). For each task run: (a) baseline verifier exemplar (syntax-only Docker oracle) and (b) guarded verifier exemplar (syntax+policy+reachability/stateful Docker oracle). Outcome per task is binary: detected/not-detected by each verifier class. Inclusion: only items with provable public provenance metadata or generated by the seeded injection scripts are included. Exclusion: items failing deterministic provenance checks or anonymization steps are automatically excluded. Randomization: confirmatory task selection and injection-variant assignment are deterministic using fixed RNG seeds. All seeds, selection lists, and logs are recorded and hashed in the execution manifest.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect delta = 0.15 (15 percentage points). Sample-size rationale: normal-approximation paired-proportion conservative variance p(1-p)=0.25 yields required N ≈ 88; preregister N=100 paired tasks to achieve ≥80% power at two-sided alpha=0.05. Planned scenario: scenario_recommended_100 (100 confirmatory pairs, 50 exploratory tasks). Post-hoc achieved-power will be reported given observed baseline rate.
exclusion_rules: Exclude any corpus item lacking a documented public source URL.
Exclude items with non-empty matches to private-identifier regex set (automated).
Exclude LLM-generated proposal if similarity hash to any excluded item > 0.9; apply deterministic re-seed policy and log event; if re-seeded output still fails, exclude task.
missingness_plan: Technical failures (e.g., runtime container crash, API outage) are detected deterministically by the execution harness and logged. Primary analysis uses complete_pair_primary: any pair with an infrastructure/technical failure is excluded and listed in the technical-failure log. Sensitivity analysis treats technical failure as detection=0 per complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity. Ambiguous verifier outputs that do not contain the canonical violation token are mapped deterministically to detection=0. No human adjudication is permitted.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis uses the registered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor computing paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (primary_estimand_id: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) with two-sided alpha=0.05. Primary failed_call_treatment = complete_pair_primary (exclude deterministic infrastructure-failure pairs). Sensitivity analysis: complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity. Binary detection mapping: verifier returns a non-empty deterministic violation trace (canonical token) → detected=1; otherwise detected=0. Analysis outputs: point estimate of paired difference, 95% CI, two-sided p-value, per-verifier-class coverage, per-failure-subclass summaries, per-task confusion matrices, and clustered detectability heatmaps. All analysis inputs (per-task binaries, seeds, logs, hashes) are stored in execution manifest.
multiplicity_plan: One preregistered primary confirmatory hypothesis (H2). Secondary and exploratory analyses (per-verifier-class, leaf-level failure subclass analyses) are exploratory and will report unadjusted p-values; where multiple exploratory tests are summarized, Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction will be presented. All exploratory findings labeled as exploratory.
contamination_plan: Benchmarks: public_netops_change_corpus_v1, llm_injection_suite_v1. Risks: inclusion of vendor-sensitive/private snippets; LLM copying verbatim from non-public sources; label leakage. Detection: provenance-check engine enforces source-URL domain whitelist; deterministic pattern scanner flags private tokens (emails, private ASNs, internal hostnames) and triggers exclusion; LLM-output similarity check using exact-substring hashing triggers deterministic re-seed/drop rules. Item-flagging rules and re-seeding are automated and logged. Analysis will report exclusions and re-seed events. Residual uncertainty: inability to prove LLM training-data provenance; documented as residual contamination risk.
stopping_rule: Stop when 100 confirmatory paired tasks (task_count) have complete paired outcomes without infrastructure failure exclusions, or when the execution harness exhausts the preregistered maximum_model_calls (200), or on certified deterministic infrastructure abort (e.g., repeated container failure) requiring run termination. All stopping events are logged and hashed.
planned_outputs: Open benchmark release: confirmatory task set (N=100), exploratory tasks (N=50), anonymized artifacts, and seeds.
Dockerized verifier oracles (syntax-only baseline exemplar and guarded exemplar) with deterministic CI tests.
Injection suite and taxonomic mapping code (seeded scripts).
Execution manifest, raw logs, analysis artifacts, and hashes for reproducibility.
Peer-reviewed CNSM short paper (IEEE format) and mandatory Disclosure Statement.
